This new land is small and the resources are scarce, so you take what you can get and never say no to building materials. Cleverly plan and construct a thriving town, and don't let it fill up with wasted resources! Whoever builds the most prosperous tiny town wins! In Tiny Towns, your town is represented by a 4x4 grid on which you will place resource cubes in specific layouts to construct buildings. Each building scores victory points (VPs) in a unique way. When no player can place any more resources or construct any buildings, the game ends, and any squares without a building are worth -1 VP. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Players take turns to be the Master Builder and call a colour of brick. Every player places a brick of that colour in an empty space on their board. If you have bricks in the same pattern as a building template (which may be mirrored, flipped or rotated) you may then choose to build that building. Click on the building's card and then click which space on your playerboard you want the building's tile to be placed. It must be one of the squares that contained a brick you used to build it. Some buildings give points, some give powers, some give both. Bricks do not have to be placed next to one another, you can start different buildings in other places. You can also leave a complete pattern of bricks unbuilt until a later turn. When a building requires another to be "adjacent", this means orthogonal (up, down, left or right) - not diagonal. Continue on until all playerboard squares are filled. You will lose points for bricks that do not form a building. Different buildings will be drawn each game. Still an incredibly dull game. Too solitaire for my taste. The player elimination can be annoying if you got eliminated early and the game drags on for the others.

[Rating: 1/10] While playing games cannot forget that AEG has poor customer service, works basically for US.

[Rating: 1/10] Boring bingo style VP optimization puzzle, I see no reason to return to this one as you've seen all the game has to offer on the first play.

[Rating: 2/10] Pick a colored cube and stick it somewhere on your board hoping to match it with various patterns selected for the game and which give you scoring opportunities.  Everyone else has to take the same colored cube and place it too.  Then the next player goes.  Complete a pattern, remove those cubes and put a building on one of those squares.  The buildings may give you end game points if they're placed just right.  The is one of the most awful, stupid, and random games I've ever played.
